Parents of Rhoam Summer share memories of 5-year-old killed in Bend shooting

=== MULTI-SOURCE TOPIC CLUSTER: Parents of Rhoam Summer share memories of 5-year-old killed in Bend shooting ===

[Source 1 — www.opb.org] (URL: https://www.opb.org/article/2026/10/19/parents-of-rhoam-summer-share-memories-of-5-year-old-killed-in-bend-shooting/):
Stated Claim / Post Context:
Parents of Rhoam Summer share memories of 5-year-old killed in Bend shooting

Kelik and Lillian Summer are asking those grieving their son’s death to turn to art.

Actual Article Body:
Independent. Member-supported.For the Pacific Northwest.

Independent.Member-supported.

An undated photo of Rhoam Summer, 5, who died in the Oct. 15, 2026, Silver Rail Elementary School shooting in Bend, Ore.

Courtesy of Bend Police Department

Rhoam Summer loved dancing, dinosaurs and making art, the parents of the 5-year-old kindergarten student killed at Silver Rail Elementary School said in a statement released through their lawyers.

Rhoam was one of three children and a teacher who died when a 16-year-old with a shotgun forced his way into a classroom on Oct. 15. The shooter was then killed by a parent who saw him enter and followed with a gun.

Now, Kelik and Lillian Summer are asking those grieving their son’s death to turn to art.

“If you want to memorialize our little Rhoam, we request you draw,” the Summers said in their statement, which was posted to Facebook Monday. “Rhoam loved to tell stories of creatures with big teeth who needed understanding and friendship. Please make art for him. Draw or paint. Use your hands if you can. Get messy.”

The youth-art-focused Bend nonprofit Hearts Unknown Education, or HÚE, says it’s hosting a painting and drawing session dedicated to Rhoam’s memory on Tuesday.

The Summers released their statement as Bend grapples with the deaths of Rhoam, two classmates, ages 8 and 11 — whose names have not been officially released — and their teacher, 25-year-old Megan Lambert.

The Summers said they understand that many in the community want to know about their son.

“His heart knew no limits, and it grew with him every single day. We were so proud of who he was and who he was growing to be,” they wrote. “He was 5 years old. He wanted to go to the pumpkin patch, learn to ride horses, learn to play an instrument, and be a bunny for Halloween.”

From his earliest days, he brought light into the world, they said.

“Rhoam was so so strong. The day he was born, his father gave him his first sink bath at the hospital. In the sink, Rhoam grabbed his dad’s hands and pulled himself up with his own strength,” the Summers wrote. “He climbed a ladder (3-step stool) when he was just 6 months old. He never stopped moving. He never stopped climbing. He could do anything.”

As he got older, Rhoam was a generous child, they said, making sure visitors to their home had a drink, or a snack, or a toy to cuddle. “He wanted to share everything he had.”

Rhoam was a child with many interests.

“He loved rainbows and unicorns from a very young age,” his parents said. “He loved sharks and dinosaurs. He cooked meals with his parents, cuddled at every opportunity, and sang to himself when he was upset. He told the sweetest, most amazing stories and was learning to give each character their own voice.”

Now the Summers are telling the story of their son.

“We could not have hoped for a more wonderful child, and everyone in his family, found family, and friend circle could not wait to see how he grew,” his parents said.

College president killed in freak accident while touring famous architect’s home

Rogério Renato Mateucci, 55, was on a group tour of Frank Lloyd Wright’s Taliesin West home in Scottsdale when strong winds dislodged a piece of roofing that struck him in the head.

Actual Article Body:
Switch between CA and NY editions here.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

A Brazilian college president was struck and killed by a piece of stray roofing in a freak accident while on an architecture tour in Arizona, officials said.

Rogério Renato Mateucci, 55, was on a group tour of Frank Lloyd Wright’s Taliesin West home in Scottsdale last Friday around 2 p.m. when strong winds gusting up to 32 mph dislodged a piece of roofing, AZ Family reported.

Mateucci, the rector of Pontifical Catholic University of Paraná in Brazil, was struck in the head by the roofing material and died instantly in what officials are labeling a weather-related accident, the outlet reported.

A spokesperson for the Frank Lloyd Wright Foundation, which is based out of the Scottsdale location, expressed their “deep condolences” following the shocking mishap.

“The property is closed to the public until further notice,” the foundation announced in a statement posted to Facebook.

Mateucci had been the Catholic university’s most senior head since 2022, the Brazilian outlet G1 reported.

The academic also held multiple degrees in education, including a doctorate from Fordham University in educational leadership, according to the publication.

Classes at the college were canceled Saturday through Monday in mourning of the rector’s passing, the Pontifical Catholic University of Paraná said in a statement.

The university also announced a Mass in memory of Mateucci would be held on Monday, with funeral arrangements to follow once his body has been repatriated to Brazil.

In a press release, the university discussed Mateucci’s death in relation to the school’s Catholic beliefs.

“And, for those who believe, life is not taken from us, but transformed. Therefore, united by faith in the resurrection, let us now join in prayer for our dearest Brother Rogério,” the university concluded.

Bridie Lee, 32, died at the scene, while Ryan Riethmuller, 39, died days later in hospital. (Supplied)

Thi Phuong Ngoc Nguyen, 40, was summonsed to appear in the ACT Magistrates Court today over a crash on Canberra's Gunghalin Drive that killed cyclists Bridie Lee and Ryan Riethmuller.

She has pleaded not guilty to two counts of culpable driving causing death and one count of negligent driving occasioning actual bodily harm.

The case is due to return to court in January 2027.

A 40-year-old woman has pleaded not guilty to charges over a double fatal collision in Canberra's north.

Bridie Lee, 32, and Ryan Riethmuller, 39, were among five cyclists struck by a blue Hyundai Accent on Gunghalin Drive in Palmerston at about 6:20am on August 27.

The group of cyclists was struck by a blue Hyundai Accent on Gunghalin Drive in Palmerston on August 27. (ABC News: Luke Stephenson)

Members of the public, including an off-duty nurse and police officer, assisted the injured cyclists while they waited for emergency services to arrive.

Ms Lee died at the scene, while Mr Riethmuller died in hospital a week later.

Bridie Lee was a member of the Canberra Bilbys Triathlon Club.  (Supplied)

The incident prompted an outpouring of grief in the cycling community, with hundreds of mourners taking part in a tribute ride for the victims who had been involved in Canberra's triathlon community.

Ryan Riethmuller was a member of the Canberra Bilbys Triathlon Club. (Supplied)

Last month, Thi Phuong Ngoc Nguyen was summonsed to appear in the ACT Magistrates court today on two counts of culpable driving causing death and one count of negligent driving occasioning actual bodily harm.

She didn't appear in person this morning, and was instead represented by her lawyer, Mitchell Greig, who entered not guilty pleas to all charges and sought a date for a pre-hearing mention.

The case is due to return to court in January next year.
